## Mock 01

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Mock-Tests/Nursing-Foundations-Mock-01-120.md` (blob `b5f0d4331417b7a1df09e7f30e569c159aac198d`).

### Q34. What is the purpose of a prescribed texture-modified diet in dysphagia?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Increase choking risk deliberately
- **B.** Replace swallowing assessment permanently
- **C.** Provide a consistency suited to the patient's assessed swallowing ability
- **D.** Ensure all patients receive exactly the same food

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Provide a consistency suited to the patient's assessed swallowing ability**

Texture modification mein food ki consistency aur liquid ki thickness assessment ke basis par adjust hoti hai. Iska goal patient ko aisi consistency dena hai jise woh comparatively safely aur efficiently swallow kar sake. Thickened liquids har patient ke liye best nahi hote aur hydration ya intake affect kar sakte hain. Prescribed texture follow karo aur tolerance reassess karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Diet ka aim choking aur unsafe swallowing ka risk kam karna hai, badhana nahi.
- **B (Galat):** Swallowing ability time ke saath badal sakti hai. Texture plan future assessment replace nahi karta.
- **C (Sahi):** Assessed ability ke hisaab se consistency select karna individualized dysphagia care ka part hai.
- **D (Galat):** Har patient ka swallowing impairment same nahi hota. Universal diet unsuitable ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Texture is prescribed after assessment, not universally thickened.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care) · [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q47. A patient who is drowsy after sedation is scheduled for oral feeding. Which action is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Use a straw regardless of swallowing plan
- **B.** Reassess alertness and swallowing safety before offering food
- **C.** Place food in the mouth while the patient is unresponsive
- **D.** Feed rapidly before the patient falls asleep

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Reassess alertness and swallowing safety before offering food**

Sedation se alertness, cough reflex aur swallowing coordination reduce ho sakti hai. Agar patient fully awake nahi hai toh food mouth mein retain ya airway mein enter ho sakta hai. Nurse meal se pehle responsiveness aur safe swallow status assess karti hai. Unsafe findings mein oral feed defer karke team ko inform karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Straw kuch patients mein helpful aur doosron mein unsuitable ho sakta hai. Assessment ke bina use mat karo.
- **B (Sahi):** Alertness aur swallow safety reassess karna aspiration risk identify karta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Unresponsive patient ko orally feed karna airway protection compromise karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Rapid feeding coordination improve nahi karti aur choking risk badha sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Alert enough and cleared to swallow before oral feeding.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q105. A patient coughs repeatedly and develops a wet voice while drinking water after stroke. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Stop oral intake temporarily, assess airway and arrange swallowing evaluation
- **B.** Give tablets with water before assessment
- **C.** Continue the meal because coughing is normal in all patients
- **D.** Encourage larger sips to improve swallowing

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Stop oral intake temporarily, assess airway and arrange swallowing evaluation**

Stroke se swallowing muscles ka control affect ho sakta hai. Repeated cough aur wet ya gurgly voice liquid ke airway ke paas pahunchne ka warning sign ho sakte hain. Oral intake rok kar airway aur breathing assess karo. Agar severe distress hai toh emergency help activate karo. Trained swallowing assessment aur safe alternative medication/nutrition plan arrange karo. Cough absent hona bhi aspiration ko rule out nahi karta.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Feeding stop karna, airway assess karna aur swallowing evaluation arrange karna patient safety prioritize karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Tablets aur water bhi aspirate ho sakte hain. Oral medication route reassess karna chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Repeated coughing ko routine maan kar feeding continue karna unsafe hai.
- **D (Galat):** Large sips patient ki swallowing capacity exceed kar sakte hain.

**Exam clue:** Cough or wet voice during intake = stop, assess, refer.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q111. A patient with impaired swallowing is about to receive a meal. Which position usually reduces aspiration risk when tolerated?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Prone without assessment
- **B.** Head-down tilt
- **C.** Upright sitting with individualized swallowing recommendations
- **D.** Flat supine

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Upright sitting with individualized swallowing recommendations**

Dysphagia ka matlab nigalne mein dikkat hai. Aspiration tab hoti hai jab food, saliva ya liquid airway mein chala jaata hai. Agar patient oral intake ke liye assessed safe hai, toh upright position aur prescribed head posture swallowing control mein help karte hain. Patient ko small manageable bites aur individualized feeding assistance do. Sirf upright bithane se unsafe swallow safe nahi ho jaata.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bina assessment prone feeding mein airway aur swallowing monitor karna difficult ho sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Head-down tilt routine oral feeding posture nahi hai aur swallowing safety compromise kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Upright sitting aur assessed swallow plan food ka control aur airway protection support karte hain. Yeh best listed choice hai.
- **D (Galat):** Flat supine mein food aur liquid ko safely control karna mushkil ho sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Position plus individualized swallow plan, not position alone.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q71. Which method best supports independence in a patient with limited hand strength during feeding?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Provide suitable adaptive utensils and assistance only as needed
- **B.** Feed the patient completely without checking ability
- **C.** Remove the meal if the patient eats slowly
- **D.** Require use of standard utensils despite difficulty

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Provide suitable adaptive utensils and assistance only as needed**

Limited hand strength mein patient spoon ko grip karne ya food ko mouth tak le jaane mein difficulty feel kar sakta hai. Adapted handle, suitable utensil aur assessed positioning se patient apna kaam jitna safely possible ho khud kar sakta hai. Nurse adequate time, dignity aur required help provide karti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Adaptive utensils grip aur control improve karte hain. Need-based assistance independence maintain karti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Ability check kiye bina complete feeding patient ki remaining skills use karne ka chance kam karti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Slow eating ki wajah se tray remove karna nutritional intake reduce kar sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Standard utensils force karne se fatigue aur frustration badh sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Promote safe self-feeding with appropriate aids.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q77. During enteral feeding, the tube's external marking changes substantially. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Increase feeding rate to compensate for interruption
- **B.** Stop feeding and re-establish placement according to protocol before further use
- **C.** Ignore the change if the patient does not cough
- **D.** Advance the tube blindly to the old marking and resume

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Stop feeding and re-establish placement according to protocol before further use**

External marking tube ke nose ke paas visible length batati hai. Marking mein major change tube migrate hone ka warning hai. Tube tip esophagus ya airway mein shift ho sakti hai. Feed aur medicines stop karo, patient assess karo aur approved method se placement dobara confirm karvao. Confirmed safe use se pehle flush ya feed resume mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Rate increase displacement correct nahi karta.
- **B (Sahi):** Feed hold aur placement re-verification wrong-route administration prevent karte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Cough absent hone se wrong placement exclude nahi hota.
- **D (Galat):** Blind advancement tube ko wrong route mein le ja sakta hai aur tissue damage kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Changed external length = hold, check, confirm before use.

**Clinical references:** [NHS England NG safety](https://www.england.nhs.uk/patient-safety/patient-safety-insight/patient-safety-alerts/enduring-standards/standards-that-remain-valid/medical-device-safety/) · [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/)

**YouTube MCQ practice lead:** [Voogly by Sahu Sir — Enteral vs Parenteral Nutrition MCQ class](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rZz7iDEj7Tg). Indexed publisher description includes enteral/parenteral routes. Direct retrieval failed, exact question coverage and playback pending.

</details>

### Q93. What is the usual purpose of flushing an enteral feeding tube with prescribed water?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Replace all nutritional requirements
- **B.** Maintain tube patency and provide ordered water when appropriate
- **C.** Sterilize the stomach
- **D.** Confirm gastric placement without other checks

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Maintain tube patency and provide ordered water when appropriate**

Patency ka matlab tube ka passage open hona hai. Formula aur medicines ke particles tube mein collect hokar blockage bana sakte hain. Prescribed water flush residue clear karne aur planned hydration mein help karta hai. Tube placement pehle verify hona chahiye. Water type aur volume route, clinical condition aur fluid allowance ke hisaab se choose karo. Resistance par forceful flushing mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Water nutrition ke calories, protein aur micronutrients provide nahi karta.
- **B (Sahi):** Appropriate flushing tube open rakhne aur ordered water dene mein help karti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Water flush stomach ko sterile nahi banata.
- **D (Galat):** Flush easily pass hone se tip stomach mein hai, yeh confirm nahi hota.

**Exam clue:** Flush for patency/hydration, not placement confirmation.

**Clinical references:** [NHS SPS medicines via enteral tubes](https://sps.nhs.uk/articles/administering-a-medicine-through-an-enteral-feeding-tube/) · [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/)

**YouTube MCQ practice lead:** [Voogly by Sahu Sir — Enteral vs Parenteral Nutrition MCQ class](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rZz7iDEj7Tg). Indexed publisher description includes enteral/parenteral routes. Direct retrieval failed, exact question coverage and playback pending.

</details>

### Q102. A newly inserted nasogastric tube is intended for feeding. Which action is essential before first use?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Inject air and rely on an abdominal whoosh alone
- **B.** Assume correct placement because the patient can speak
- **C.** Use the tube immediately if its external length seems correct
- **D.** Confirm placement using the approved evidence-based method and document authorization for use

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: D. Confirm placement using the approved evidence-based method and document authorization for use**

Nasogastric ya NG tube nose se stomach tak jaane ke liye insert hoti hai, lekin galti se airway mein bhi ja sakti hai. Feed, medicine ya flush dene se pehle approved placement confirmation zaroori hai. NHS England standard mein approved gastric aspirate pH 1–5.5 ya appropriately interpreted X-ray acceptable hain. Agar aspirate unavailable ya pH unsafe ho toh protocol ke mutabik X-ray ya escalation chahiye. Kuch settings initial X-ray require karti hain. Documented clearance se pehle tube mein kuch introduce mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Air inject karke whoosh sunna reliable location test nahi hai. Airway tube mein bhi misleading sound mil sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Patient speak kar paaye toh bhi tube respiratory tract mein ho sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** External length insertion estimate deta hai, tip ki actual location prove nahi karta.
- **D (Sahi):** Evidence-based placement confirmation aur documentation wrong-route feeding se harm prevent karte hain.

**Exam clue:** No first use before approved placement confirmation. Never rely on whoosh.

**Clinical references:** [NHS England NG safety](https://www.england.nhs.uk/patient-safety/patient-safety-insight/patient-safety-alerts/enduring-standards/standards-that-remain-valid/medical-device-safety/) · [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/)

**YouTube MCQ practice lead:** [Voogly by Sahu Sir — Enteral vs Parenteral Nutrition MCQ class](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rZz7iDEj7Tg). Indexed publisher description includes enteral/parenteral routes. Direct retrieval failed, exact question coverage and playback pending.

</details>

### Q29. Which information should be included when monitoring nutritional intake?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Only the amount delivered on the tray
- **B.** The food preferences of the neighboring patient
- **C.** Actual amount consumed and relevant tolerance findings
- **D.** Assume the full meal was eaten if the tray is removed

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Actual amount consumed and relevant tolerance findings**

Nutritional intake delivered food se nahi, actual consumed amount se assess hoti hai. Nurse portion ya measured volume, supplements, nausea, vomiting, chewing/swallowing difficulty aur relevant assistance record karti hai. Isse dietitian ko nutrition plan adjust karne ke liye accurate trend milta hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Tray par delivered food ka matlab patient ne sab consume kiya, yeh nahi hai.
- **B (Galat):** Neighboring patient ki preference is patient ke intake ko measure nahi karti.
- **C (Sahi):** Actual consumed amount aur tolerance record karna nutritional monitoring ka useful part hai.
- **D (Galat):** Tray removal par full consumption assume karne se false record ban sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** Record what the patient actually consumed, not what was served.

**Clinical references:** [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations) · [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

</details>

### Q52. Which practice is appropriate when administering several compatible prescribed medicines through an enteral tube?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Skip all flushes to save time
- **B.** Crush every medication together into the feeding formula
- **C.** Verify each formulation and give separately with appropriate flushes according to policy
- **D.** Use an IV syringe connected to an enteral line

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Verify each formulation and give separately with appropriate flushes according to policy**

Enteral medicine tube se gut mein jaati hai. Har drug ka formulation aur tube compatibility alag ho sakti hai. Modified-release ya enteric-coated medicines ko bina pharmacist review crush karna unsafe ho sakta hai. Each medicine separately prepare aur administer karo, compatible enteral syringe use karo aur before, between aur after prescribed flushes do. Feed interruption medicine-specific interaction ke hisaab se decide hota hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Flush skip karne se medicine residue aur blockage risk badh sakta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Sab medicines crush karke formula mein mix karna dose delivery aur interactions ko affect kar sakta hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Formulation verify karna, separate administration aur suitable flushes safe practice support karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** IV syringe ko enteral line se connect karna wrong-route error ka risk badhata hai.

**Exam clue:** Separate medicines, enteral connector, appropriate flushes.

**Clinical references:** [NHS SPS medicines via enteral tubes](https://sps.nhs.uk/articles/administering-a-medicine-through-an-enteral-feeding-tube/)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q59. A patient has severe malnutrition and is about to restart nutrition. Which electrolyte disturbance is particularly associated with refeeding syndrome?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Hyperphosphatemia as the typical defining early shift
- **B.** Hypophosphatemia
- **C.** Isolated high sodium in every patient
- **D.** Guaranteed normal electrolyte levels

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Hypophosphatemia**

Severe malnutrition mein body prolonged low intake ke according adapt ho jaati hai. Jab calories dobara milti hain, insulin rise se phosphate, potassium aur magnesium cells ke andar shift ho sakte hain. Hypophosphatemia ka matlab blood phosphate low hona hai. Severe decrease energy production, muscles, breathing aur heart function ko affect kar sakta hai. Risk assessment, thiamine, electrolyte checks, prescribed cautious nutrition advancement aur monitoring zaroori hain.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Early refeeding mein phosphate commonly fall kar sakta hai, rise typical hallmark nahi hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Hypophosphatemia refeeding syndrome ki characteristic electrolyte disturbance hai. Potassium aur magnesium bhi monitor karo.
- **C (Galat):** Sodium aur fluid balance change ho sakte hain, lekin isolated high sodium defining electrolyte finding nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** High-risk patients mein electrolyte abnormalities develop ho sakti hain even if baseline normal ho.

**Exam clue:** Refeeding risk: phosphate, potassium, magnesium and thiamine.

**Clinical references:** [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q79. An enterally fed patient develops sudden coughing, breathlessness and oxygen desaturation. Which action is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Lay the patient flat and continue formula
- **B.** Increase feeding rate
- **C.** Stop feeding, assess and support breathing and seek urgent help
- **D.** Wait until the current bag empties

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Stop feeding, assess and support breathing and seek urgent help**

Sudden coughing, breathlessness aur oxygen saturation drop acute respiratory compromise ke signs hain. Enteral feed aspiration ek possibility hai, lekin other acute causes bhi assess karne hain. Feed immediately stop karo, airway aur breathing assess/support karo aur urgent help activate karo. Patient ki condition ke hisaab se safe positioning, oxygen aur suction trained protocol ke mutabik use ho sakte hain. Reassessment se pehle feed restart mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Flat position aur continued feed respiratory safety compromise kar sakte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Faster feeding possible aspiration ko worsen kar sakti hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Feed stop aur urgent breathing assessment further exposure aur deterioration ka risk kam karte hain.
- **D (Galat):** Bag finish hone ka wait acute respiratory problem ka treatment delay karta hai.

**Exam clue:** Sudden respiratory deterioration during feeding = stop feed, ABC, urgent help.

**Clinical references:** [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/) · [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q3. Which is a key advantage of enteral nutrition when the gastrointestinal tract is functional and accessible?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** It uses the gastrointestinal tract and supports gut function
- **B.** It always eliminates aspiration risk
- **C.** It never requires placement verification
- **D.** It provides nutrition directly into an artery

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. It uses the gastrointestinal tract and supports gut function**

Enteral nutrition mein nutrients gastrointestinal tract yani stomach ya intestine ke through deliver hote hain. Jab gut functional aur accessible ho, enteral route gut use aur mucosal function support kar sakta hai. Route selection swallowing safety, absorption, clinical stability aur tolerance ke hisaab se hoti hai. Enteral tube bhi aspiration risk ko zero nahi karti.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** Gut ka use enteral nutrition ki defining feature aur important advantage hai.
- **B (Galat):** Tube-fed patient reflux, secretions ya misplaced tube se aspirate kar sakta hai.
- **C (Galat):** Feeding tube ko approved placement verification chahiye.
- **D (Galat):** Artery mein nutrient dena enteral route nahi hai aur routine nutrition delivery ka appropriate route bhi nahi hai.

**Exam clue:** Functional accessible gut supports enteral route when clinically appropriate.

**Clinical references:** [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations) · [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/)

### Q5. Which measurement helps monitor longer-term nutritional and fluid trends when obtained under consistent conditions?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** The patient's bed number
- **B.** Serial body weight
- **C.** A single room temperature reading
- **D.** The number of available meal trays

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Serial body weight**

Serial weight ka matlab same patient ka weight repeated times par record karna hai. Same scale aur comparable time/clothing conditions se measurement variation kam hoti hai. Weight trend nutritional progress ya fluid gain/loss suggest kar sakta hai. Edema aur dehydration weight ko affect karte hain, isliye clinical findings aur intake ke saath interpret karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Bed number administrative identification hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Consistent serial body weight clinically useful trend provide karta hai, lekin fluid status ko bhi consider karna chahiye.
- **C (Galat):** Room temperature patient ka nutrition ya fluid trend directly measure nahi karta.
- **D (Galat):** Tray count available meals batata hai, body weight change nahi.

**Exam clue:** Same conditions for repeated weights. Weight gain can be fluid.

**Clinical references:** [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q43. A patient receiving parenteral nutrition through a central line develops fever and rigors. Which response is appropriate?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Mix an unprescribed antibiotic into the nutrition bag
- **B.** Assess urgently for possible bloodstream infection and follow line and sepsis protocols
- **C.** Assume fever is a normal nutrient response
- **D.** Ignore the findings until the infusion finishes

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Assess urgently for possible bloodstream infection and follow line and sepsis protocols**

Parenteral nutrition nutrients ko venous circulation ke through deliver karti hai. Central line ke through germs bloodstream tak pahunch sakte hain. Rigors yani intense shaking chills aur fever possible bloodstream infection ke signs hain. Vitals aur perfusion urgently assess karo, sepsis pathway activate karo if indicated aur line management/cultures prescribed protocol se arrange karo. Antibiotic khud se nutrition bag mein mix mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Unprescribed antibiotic mixing sterility, compatibility aur dose safety compromise karti hai.
- **B (Sahi):** Urgent assessment aur line/sepsis protocol infection aur deterioration ko timely address karte hain.
- **C (Galat):** Fever aur rigors ko routine nutrient response assume karna dangerous ho sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Infusion khatam hone ka wait possible sepsis treatment delay karta hai.

**Exam clue:** PN + fever/rigors = assess promptly for catheter-related infection and other causes.

**Clinical references:** [Catheter bloodstream infection in parenteral nutrition](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6914297/) · [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)

</details>

### Q59. A patient on continuous enteral nutrition has an interruption because of a procedure and receives glucose-lowering medication. Which risk should the nurse consider?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Guaranteed hyperglycemia in every case
- **B.** Immediate protein overload
- **C.** Hypoglycemia if medication effect continues without the expected carbohydrate delivery
- **D.** No need for monitoring because feeding has stopped

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Hypoglycemia if medication effect continues without the expected carbohydrate delivery**

Continuous feed carbohydrate supply deti hai. Agar feed interrupt ho jaaye lekin insulin ya hypoglycemia-causing medicine active rahe, glucose low ho sakta hai. Nurse blood glucose promptly check karti hai aur prescribed feed-interruption protocol follow karti hai. Authorized plan mein nutritional insulin adjustment ya dextrose support ho sakta hai. Type 1 diabetes mein basal insulin ko automatically stop mat karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Hyperglycemia guaranteed nahi hai. Glucose response patient aur therapy par depend karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Feed interruption immediate protein overload ka typical mechanism nahi hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Carbohydrate delivery rukne aur active insulin/medicine effect ke mismatch se hypoglycemia ho sakti hai.
- **D (Galat):** Feed rukne par active medication ke saath monitoring aur important ho sakti hai.

**Exam clue:** Feed interrupted + active insulin = hypoglycemia risk, monitor and follow protocol.

**Clinical references:** [ADA 2026 hospital diabetes care](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-s016)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

## Mock 05

Source: `Chapters/Nursing-Foundations/Mock-Tests/Nursing-Foundations-Mock-05-120.md` (blob `c6caf7eb0ae9cfe1d9886432a34c4fca264da21c`).

### Q28. Which intervention supports oral health in a patient who is not eating by mouth?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Use oral care as a replacement for prescribed nutrition
- **B.** Provide regular individualized oral care despite the NPO order
- **C.** Avoid oral hygiene until oral meals resume
- **D.** Give unapproved water to drink despite aspiration restrictions

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: B. Provide regular individualized oral care despite the NPO order**

NPO ka matlab nil per os yani mouth se food, drink ya medicines restricted as ordered. Iska matlab mouth care band karna nahi hai. Oral bacteria, dryness aur plaque accumulate ho sakte hain. Assessed oral hygiene aur aspiration precautions ke saath mouth clean rakho, zarurat par trained suction-assisted care use karo. Water swallow karne ki permission NPO order se alag verify hoti hai.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Oral hygiene nutrition ke calories aur nutrients supply nahi karti.
- **B (Sahi):** Regular individualized oral care comfort aur oral health improve karti hai, even if patient NPO hai.
- **C (Galat):** Oral hygiene stop karne se plaque, dryness aur bacterial burden badh sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Unapproved water aspiration restriction violate kar sakta hai.

**Exam clue:** NPO does not mean no oral care.

**Clinical references:** [Canadian Stroke Best Practices](https://www.strokebestpractices.ca/recommendations/stroke-rehabilitation-delivery/6-swallowing-nutrition-and-oral-care)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q32. A patient has a new prescription for nutritional supplementation but reports a severe allergy to an ingredient. What should the nurse do?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Give a small trial dose without authorization
- **B.** Remove the allergy alert because it is food-related
- **C.** Withhold the product until the ingredient and safe alternatives are verified
- **D.** Dilute the supplement and assume the allergen is harmless

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: C. Withhold the product until the ingredient and safe alternatives are verified**

Food allergy mein immune system specific ingredient ko harmful samajhkar reaction kar sakta hai. Severe reaction anaphylaxis tak progress kar sakti hai, jisme breathing ya circulation affect hoti hai. Product hold karo, ingredient list aur allergy record verify karo aur prescriber/dietitian se safe alternative arrange karo. Cross-contact risk bhi consider karo. Reaction develop ho toh urgent emergency protocol follow karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Galat):** Unauthorized trial dose even small amount mein severe reaction trigger kar sakti hai.
- **B (Galat):** Food allergy bhi important safety alert hai. Alert remove karna future exposure ka risk badhata hai.
- **C (Sahi):** Withhold and verify ingredients, allergy history and safe alternative exposure prevent karta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Dilution allergen ko remove nahi karti aur reaction ka risk rehta hai.

**Exam clue:** Known severe allergy = hold and verify before administration.

**Clinical references:** [FDA food allergy safety](https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-food-labeling-and-critical-foods/food-allergies)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q71. Which action is appropriate when a patient has a prescribed fluid restriction and receives enteral tube flushes?

**Difficulty:** Difficult | **Priority:** High

- **A.** Count flush water and other measurable fluids toward the ordered allowance
- **B.** Stop essential flushes without obtaining a plan
- **C.** Increase flush volume without reviewing the order
- **D.** Exclude all tube flushes from intake

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Count flush water and other measurable fluids toward the ordered allowance**

Tube flush mein diya gaya water patient ke total fluid intake ka part hai. Fluid restriction heart, renal ya doosri conditions mein fluid accumulation control karne ke liye prescribe ho sakti hai. Formula water content, flush water, medicines ke saath water aur other measurable fluids local accounting plan ke mutabik track karo. Essential flushes ka safe volume dietitian/prescriber ke saath coordinate karo.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** All relevant measured fluid count karna accurate balance aur safe restriction plan support karta hai.
- **B (Galat):** Essential flush stop karne se blockage aur medicine delivery problem ho sakti hai.
- **C (Galat):** Bina order volume increase prescribed allowance exceed kar sakta hai.
- **D (Galat):** Flush exclude karne se total intake underestimate hota hai.

**Exam clue:** Flushes count toward fluid intake. Coordinate required patency volumes.

**Clinical references:** [NHS SPS medicines via enteral tubes](https://sps.nhs.uk/articles/administering-a-medicine-through-an-enteral-feeding-tube/) · [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)

**Dedicated YouTube MCQ practice:** verification pending.

</details>

### Q104. Which observation is particularly important when assessing tolerance of enteral feeding?

**Difficulty:** Medium | **Priority:** Medium

- **A.** Nausea, abdominal discomfort or distension, stool pattern and respiratory symptoms
- **B.** Only whether the feeding bag is transparent
- **C.** Only the patient's hair color
- **D.** The brand of the bedside table

<details><summary>Answer aur explanation dekho</summary>

**Correct: A. Nausea, abdominal discomfort or distension, stool pattern and respiratory symptoms**

Enteral feed tolerance assess karte waqt patient ke symptoms important hote hain. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort/distension, stool pattern aur respiratory change feed intolerance ya another problem indicate kar sakte hain. Findings ko trend, medicines, hydration aur clinical condition ke saath assess karo. Acute respiratory symptoms mein immediate safety action chahiye, sirf routine charting nahi.

**Option-wise explanation:**
- **A (Sahi):** GI aur respiratory symptoms clinically relevant indicators hain jo further assessment guide karte hain.
- **B (Galat):** Bag transparency equipment feature hai, patient tolerance ka proof nahi.
- **C (Galat):** Hair color enteral feeding tolerance se directly related nahi hai.
- **D (Galat):** Bedside table ka brand GI ya respiratory tolerance measure nahi karta.

**Exam clue:** Assess GI and respiratory tolerance, not equipment appearance alone.

**Clinical references:** [Open RN enteral tube management](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK593216/) · [NICE CG32 nutrition support](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg32/chapter/Recommendations)
